tasks.short: Inspect crops for maturity, disease or insect infestation.

steps.what: Walk the crop and see maturity, disease or insects.
Type the block, the date and the finding.
Match the finding to a signed care card.

loop.input: the finding note and care cards the manager has already signed
loop.output: one card id, or no match
loop.check: the card must name the same crop and the same symptom words; else no match
loop.stop: one pass; a new symptom is left unmatched
loop.why_not_simpler: a keyword list misses a card that uses a different word for the same symptom

steps.what: Confirm or reject that match in the field.
Issue a treatment order from the confirmed finding.

tasks.design: The walk stays the manager's. A finding note on {OPS_SYSTEM} holds block, date and what was seen. A pass over signed care cards in {DOCS} may name one card, and is discarded when the crop or the symptom does not match. The manager confirms in the field. A treatment order is filed only from that confirmation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes lived in a pocket book, and a diagnosis was whatever the manager remembered from last season.
tasks.enabler_now: Block, date and a short finding are a form. Matching a card is a check against cards already signed.
tasks.still_hard: A new pest, or a crop that looks wrong for a reason no card names, is still a walk and a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can tell a ripe block from a sick one, and can refuse a match that would spray the wrong thing.
tasks.altitude: Writing the finding takes less time. The walk and the confirmation stay. The manager does not hand diagnosis to a match.

reach.task: Apply only a treatment the manager confirmed
reach.learn: Which finding was confirmed on that block

evidence.claim: A form with block, date and finding stops a blank note. Matching a signed card is not a diagnosis.
A wrong spray can breach a label condition. The source pack does not name the farm statute, so the order stays a signed step.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager walks and confirms. Workers apply a treatment only after that order. Care cards are signed elsewhere and are read, not rewritten, here.
Structured input: block id, date, crop, symptom words the manager typed. Producer is the manager on the walk. A note with no block id is rejected.
The match proposes nothing when no signed card fits. Confirmation time stays on the walk.
unknowns: Are care cards already signed and named by crop?
How often is a finding not on any card?
research_questions: Which symptoms were sprayed from memory with no note?

already_counted.description: Confirming the match is already the remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Retire a care card the manager no longer trusts.

approvals.approved_version: finding the manager confirmed on that block and date

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If findings stay in a pocket book, the match never runs and the walk is unchanged. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Examine stock for disease or parasites, and order treatment.

steps.what: Examine the animal for disease or parasites.
Record the signs against the animal id.
Decide to treat, isolate or call a veterinarian.
Write the treatment order from the signed protocol.

tasks.design: The examination stays in person. Signs are fields on the animal in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The manager decides treat, isolate or call. The order copies product, dose and withdrawal days from a protocol already signed in {DOCS}, and only for the decision just made.
tasks.previous_blocker: The exam was a memory and a bottle from the cabinet, with withdrawal days easy to miss.
tasks.enabler_now: Animal id, signs and a decision are a form. Dose and withdrawal days are already on a signed protocol.
tasks.still_hard: A sick animal that does not match a protocol, and the choice to call a veterinarian, stay a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The manager sees the animal and carries the withdrawal promise to the buyer.
tasks.altitude: The note and the order take less rewriting. The examination and the decision stay. Withdrawal days are copied, not invented.

reach.learn: Which product and which withdrawal days apply to that animal

evidence.claim: A protocol with product, dose and withdrawal days can fill an order. It cannot examine an animal.
Medicine residues are a legal limit in many countries. The source pack does not name the farm statute, so the order stays tied to a signed protocol.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager examines and decides. A veterinarian, when called, is outside this task. Workers give only the ordered product.
Structured input: animal id, signs, decision (treat, isolate or call). Producer is the manager at the exam. An order is refused when the protocol has no row for that product.
No dose is calculated here. The protocol already holds it.
unknowns: Is there a signed protocol with withdrawal days?
research_questions: How often is a dose later corrected after the animal was treated?

already_counted.description: The examination is already the remaining time on that step.
The treat or isolate decision is already remaining time.

incremental.description: Update withdrawal days when the protocol version changes.

approvals.approved_version: care decision the manager made for that animal

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If animals have no stable ids, the note is still typed and the exam is unchanged. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose crops or stock from budgets, incentives, markets and soil.

steps.what: Pull budget, incentive, soil and sales figures.
Draft a crop mix that uses only those figures.

loop.input: the constraint table: hectares, budget, incentive windows, soil limits, sales
loop.output: a mix whose hectares and costs quote that table
loop.check: hectares must sum to the usable total, and every price must be a table price; else discard
loop.stop: one draft; a missing incentive is left blank, not guessed
loop.why_not_simpler: the choice among feasible mixes is not arithmetic

steps.what: Weigh soil, incentives and the owner's directive.
Publish the year's crop and stock plan.

tasks.design: Budgets, incentive windows, soil limits and last year's sales are a table from {ERP} and {DATA_PLATFORM}. A draft mix is kept only when hectares sum to the usable total and every price is in the table. The manager weighs soil, the incentive and any directive, then publishes the year plan on {OPS_SYSTEM}. Price splits of hectares already chosen are a different task.
tasks.previous_blocker: The mix lived in a workbook only the manager could follow, rebuilt once a year from memory.
tasks.enabler_now: Hectares, prices and dated incentive windows are rows a query can show. The draft can be checked against that table.
tasks.still_hard: Soil that a test does not capture, and a directive that is not written down, stay a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which block fails in a wet year, and which incentive is not worth the constraint.

ambition.what: Revisit the mix when an incentive window opens, not only once a year.

tasks.altitude: Collecting the figures takes less time. The choice stays. The plan is published when the manager signs it, including mid-year when a window opens.

reach.task: Plant what the annual plan names
reach.learn: Which crop is on which block this year

evidence.claim: A table of hectares, prices and dated windows can be summed and checked. It does not choose the crop.
Incentive schemes are public rules with dates. The source pack does not name a farm scheme, so the window is data the firm types, not a guessed subsidy.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager chooses the mix. Finance owns the budget lines. Soil tests arrive as rows. A hectare split by price, once the crop is chosen, is the other plan task.
Structured input: block id, usable hectares, crop, budget amount, incentive name, open date, close date, soil limit, sales volume. Producer is the book and the test file. A blank price is not filled.
Drafting time is not the decision. The manager's weighing stays.
unknowns: Are incentive windows stored as dates, or only as letters?
Who may override a soil limit?
research_questions: How often does the mix change after planting has started?

already_counted.description: Weighing the mix is already the remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Retire incentive rows when the window closes.

approvals.approved_version: mix the manager chose for that year

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If incentives are unscanned letters, the table is incomplete and the manager reads them. The weighing stays. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set and apply policies for operations, maintenance and safety.

steps.what: Read incidents and the current written rule.
Write the changed safety policy in the manager's words.
File that signed version and ask for a receipt.
Brief workers on the new rule, on site.

tasks.design: Incidents and the current policy sit in {DOCS}. The manager writes the change. {WORKFLOW} files that version and records who opened it. The briefing on site stays the manager's. A model does not draft the rule.
tasks.previous_blocker: The rule was a page in a folder, and nobody could say which version the crew had seen.
tasks.enabler_now: A version and a read receipt are ordinary record fields. The words of the rule are not.
tasks.still_hard: What the rule should forbid, after an incident, is still the manager's judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which rule the crew will actually follow, and which one will be ignored.
tasks.altitude: Finding the current version takes less hunting. Writing the rule and briefing the crew stay. The manager does not gain a right to skip the briefing.

reach.learn: Which safety rule is in force this week

evidence.claim: A versioned policy with a read receipt is a records pattern. It does not decide the rule.
The source pack names a Dutch works-council rule for some staff rules. Other countries differ. Safety wording stays the manager's.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager writes and signs the policy. Workers read it and work to it. Maintenance standards are the same record, not a second system.
Structured input: policy id, version, incident ids the manager cited, effective date. Producer is the manager. A version with no effective date is not published.
No generated sentence is part of this design. Upkeep is retiring old versions.
unknowns: Is there one policy register, or several folders?
Who else must sign a safety rule?
research_questions: Which incidents never produced a written change?

already_counted.description: Writing the rule is already the remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Retire versions that are no longer in force.

approvals.approved_version: policy text the manager signed, with its version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the policy stays a paper folder, the receipt cannot be recorded and the writing is unchanged. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Walks, stock exams and the wording of a safety rule stay with the manager. The year's crop and stock plan is a signed choice, not a score. Treatment orders copy a protocol and do not invent a dose.
reach: Workers apply only a confirmed treatment.
The crew plants the published year plan.
skills_to_grow: Refuse a care-card match that does not fit the crop.
Write a rule the crew will follow, then brief it on site.
role.ambitious_version: A finding has a block and a confirmation, and the year plan can be revisited when an incentive window opens.

job.title: Farmers, Ranchers, and Other Agricultural Managers
